title: Automated profile-fusion and drift-aware benchmark suite for kernel/attention scheduling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current benchmark harness slices workload sources (prod traces, synthetic suites, fuzzed inputs) independently which masks compound regressions that only appear when realistic traffic mixes change over time. The kernel selection and attention scheduling stack shows intermittent tail regressions post-deploy when workload drift introduces longer prefix distributions or more diverse tokenization shapes. This ticket creates an automated 'profile fusion' pipeline that constructs drift-aware benchmark cohorts and enforces CI latency/cost contracts for prefill+decode scheduling and kernel routing changes.

Goals:
- Ingest live production traces, golden synthetic seeds, and randomized fuzz corpus to produce fused workload cohorts with metadata (seq_len, prefix/common-kv-length, temperature-like sampling of decode shapes).
- Define drift metrics (distribution shift on seq_len, KV cache reuse rate, tokenization bucket shifts) and auto-generate new cohort candidates when drift exceeds thresholds.
- Add CI perf gates that validate: p50/p95/p99 latency vs baseline, token cost per thousand, and tail-regression detection across cohorts.
- Integrate with kernel selection tests: validate chosen kernel variants for each cohort and add warning+block when kernel change increases tail latency beyond contract.
- Make the harness fast-to-run locally (sub-minute smoke) and reproducible in CI with deterministic seeds and stable golden seeds registry.
acceptance_criteria: Profile-fusion pipeline producing at least 5 fused cohorts (interactive, assistant-chat-like, long-prefill, short-prefill-high-decode, heavy-tokenization) with metadata attached
Drift detector emits cohort-create events and posts PRs to the benchmark catalog when seq_len or kv_reuse drift > 8%
CI perf gate setup: enforced p95 and p99 contracts in circleci or github actions for runtime-1.22 PRs; failing PRs block merge with clear regression diffs
Kernel selection check runs as part of CI: for any kernel variant swap, perf delta report highlights cohort-level latencies and a suggested fallback policy if regressions observed
Local runner reproduces a golden baseline with seed-locking and produces identical p95 within 1% across 3 runs on the same infra
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): build ingestion adapters for prod traces (sampler for 1% traffic), synthetic golden seeds, and fuzz corpus; define canonical cohort schema. Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement fusion algorithm (weighted stratified sampling), attach metadata and storage in /bench-catalog; add deterministic seed locking. Phase 3 (2 weeks): drift detection lambda and cohort auto-PR generator; dashboard for drift signals. Phase 4 (2 weeks): CI perf gates implementation + kernel-selection check and playbook for blocked merges. Phase 5 (buffer week): rollout, docs, and developer onboarding.
rollout_plan: Start behind a feature flag for runtime-1.22 branch: run fused cohorts nightly on staging; after 1 week of stable baselines, flip CI perf gates on for non-critical repos, then expand to core repos. Communicate with platform and runtime teams via #runtime-perf before enabling blocking merges. Create a rollback procedure using the golden baseline registry.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Risk: Fusion may overfit to recent traffic and underrepresent rare long-tail cases. Mitigation: keep a fixed set of golden seeds and fuzz corpus to preserve tail coverage.
- Tradeoff: Strict CI gates can slow developer velocity. Mitigation: quick local smoke runner and informative failure artifacts (perf diffs, flamegraphs) to speed triage.
- Risk: Increased CI cost due to larger cohorts. Mitigation: tiered gate: smoke fast gates for PRs, full cohort runs nightly with automatic alerting.
- Tradeoff: Sensor thresholds (drift %) require tuning — start conservative and iterate.
metrics: Baseline p50/p95/p99 for each cohort (stored in bench-catalog), mean token-cost delta, #blocked PRs due to perf regressions, drift-alert frequency, time-to-fix after blocked merge
notes: Related artifacts: confluence design doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Profile+Fusion+Design), benchmark catalog proto (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bfakedrive/bench-catalog), dashboard (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/combined-cohorts), initial spike PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2839).
